title: Convolution: filters, stride, padding and pooling

videos.script: The network of lesson 9 reads a digit as sixty-four numbers in a row. {{row}} It has no idea that two pixels sit side by side. Shuffle every image the same way, and it can learn just as well. {{shuffle}} A convolution reads the picture as a picture. It takes nine weights, a three by three filter, and slides it over the image. {{slide}} At each place it multiplies, adds, and writes down one number. The same nine weights are used everywhere. {{same}} So a stroke is found in the top corner or the bottom one, by one filter. {{edge}} This lesson does that by hand first, on one digit, in NumPy. {{numbers}} Then it measures what stride and padding do to the size, and what pooling keeps. {{sizes}} Then it trains a small convolutional network against the dense one. {{race}} On the same validation images, the dense network reaches 95.3 per cent. The convolutional one reaches 98.3. {{result}} At the end, you look inside its first layer, at sixteen filters nobody drew. {{filters}}
